correctness.rationale: The cubic graph is simple for n>=7 and the bipartite crossing count implies |D|>=n with equality iff each vertex has exactly one opposite-sign neighbor. The two ring choices attain n. The spin-neighbor equations are equivalent to that equality condition; elimination and a checked exact Laurent factorization restrict the outer cyclic Fourier modes to order 1, 4 or 5. Coprime periods and the binary additive rigidity lemma preclude mixed period twenty. Enumerating cyclic words with no singleton run yields two constants, four period-four, and ten period-five solutions, each checked against both original equations. The proof handles every n>=7, and the independent full original-adjacency enumeration at n=7,8,9 and complete 2^20 word census confirm the boundary behavior.

originality.rationale: The exact statement classifies every labelled equality configuration for one-limited vertex domination on GP(n,3), equivalently every perfect two-coloring with matrix [[2,1],[1,2]]. The general cubic-graph half-order/equality theorem supplies only the bound and a perfect-crossing characterization; the 2016 GP(n,k) article proves existence of the matrix, and the 2022 GP(n,3) article enumerates which matrices can arise rather than the number or complete structure of their realizations. Full comparison of the 2022 article, the 2016 author full text, recent cubic-graph source, related ordinary domination and the exact published-finding corpus queries did not yield a covering count. This is a best-knowledge priority assessment, not proof of publication novelty.
residual_risks: 2026 arXiv:2610.01796 full text was unavailable; its abstract concerns another cubic family, but not all comparisons can be definitive.
An equivalent complete labelled A1-coloring enumeration may exist under equitable partitions, perfect matching cuts, disconnected 2-factors, or coding theory terms not located in the bounded search.
The 2022 introduction mentions two GP(9,3) examples; that single instance is treated as known rather than as novel.

value.rationale: The numerical optimum n follows already from generic theory, but a complete all-optima classification was missing for this natural graph family. The exact multiplicity undergoes two arithmetic transitions at 4|n and 5|n, with no extra mixed configurations at 20|n. The additive binary rigidity is a structural mechanism linking spectral period restrictions with discrete combinatorial classification; it motivates the exact sequence and may inform enumeration of other matching-cut/equitable-coloring families.
